2609.23853.title: From UNDRR Reports to Event Records: Schema-Constrained LLM Extraction of Georeferenced Disasters
2609.23853.paper_summary: Disaster-risk-reduction archives describe hazard events in prose that databases such as EM-DAT (Delforge et al., 2025) cannot ingest directly. We present an LLM pipeline that generates candidate georeferenced event records using a controlled hazard vocabulary and fixed schema, retaining evidence for review. Applied to 10,000 documents from PreventionWeb, the knowledge hub managed by UNDRR, it produced 3,572 records from 1,913 documents across 24 hazard types and resolved 81% of location mentions to OpenStreetMap geometries. On 171 human-positive document windows from a stratified 217-document reference set, GPT-5 achieved 86.0% pooled attribute $F_1$, versus 44.2% for the spaCy-gazetteer baseline. Evaluation pools hazard families, location strings, and event years within documents, without assessing their assignment to individual events. GPT-5.4 ranked highest among ten LLMs (86.6% $F_1$). Verbatim evidence occurrence was 72.0% for GPT-5 and 47.2% for GPT-5.4, measuring textual traceability without establishing attribute support. We report production failure modes and automated label and location-rule compliance checks. Prompts, schema, and outputs will be released for adaptation to national reporting archives.
2609.23853.paper_summary_zh: 災害風險減少檔案以散文形式描述危害事件，這些數據庫如 EM-DAT (Delforge et al., 2025) 無法直接導入。我們提出了一個 LLM 管道，使用受控的危害詞彙和固定的架構生成候選的地理參考事件記錄，並保留證據以供審查。應用於 UNDRR 管理的知識中心 PreventionWeb 的 10,000 份文件，從 1,913 份文件中產生了 3,572 條記錄，涵蓋 24 種危害類型，並將 81% 的地點提及解析為 OpenStreetMap 幾何圖形。在來自分層的 217 份文件參考集中的 171 個人類正面文件窗口中，GPT-5 的池化屬性 $F_1$ 達到 86.0%，而 spaCy-gazetteer 基準則為 44.2%。評估池涵蓋文件中的危害類別、地點字符串和事件年份，而不評估它們對個別事件的分配。GPT-5.4 在十個 LLM 中排名最高（86.6% $F_1$）。GPT-5 的逐字證據出現率為 72.0%，而 GPT-5.4 為 47.2%，測量文本可追溯性而不建立屬性支持。我們報告了生產失敗模式和自動標籤及位置規則合規檢查。提示、架構和輸出將被釋放以適應國家報告檔案。
